policy: A kernel singleton whose private state is a linked list may not be duplicated. Either the reconstruction or the stock unit owns kernel/timeout.c, never both.

why_now.observed: rpmsg_get_endpoint on CPUNET never terminates (53,146,996 of 53,529,158 instructions at 2.0 s); the app core therefore logs 'ipc_service: Endpoint not registered' + 'bt_hci_driver: Failed to send (err -2)' at t = 5.093 s and panics in net/buf.c:467.

measurement.victim: backend_data_0 (0x21001cf8, ipc_rpmsg_static_vrings backend instance); the corrupted words are rpmsg_inst.endpoint[0].ep.node.prev (+0x38) and rvdev.rdev.ns_ept.node.next (+0x11c). Struct offsets read from the build's own DWARF: backend_data_t.rpmsg_inst.rvdev.rdev.endpoints = +0xe0.

manifest_functions.identification: The reconstruction's own header states the identity: 'Zephyr sys_clock_elapsed @ 0x010317c0'; body is z_nrf_rtc_timer_read() - last_count with last_count pinned at 0x21002b80.

Already recorded as z_add_timeout by two independent ownership records in this repository: recon/ownership/net_kernel_private_stock_adoption.json call_target_checks[4] (caller z_reset_time_slice @0x01036f24 +52) and recon/ownership/net_zephyr_stock_atomic_adoption.json call_target_checks[269] (caller z_timer_expiration_handler @0x010382fc +174). Body matches upstream statement for statement: K_FOREVER early return, sys_dnode_is_linked assert, to->fn = fn, LOCKED(&timeout_lock), absolute-vs-relative dticks, ordered insert with dticks subtraction, sys_dlist_append, sys_clock_set_timeout(next_timeout(), false).

LOCKED(&timeout_lock) { if (sys_dnode_is_linked(&to->node)) { remove_timeout(to); ret = 0; } } with ret initialised to -EINVAL (-22) - byte-for-byte the upstream shape; the same timeout_lock literal 0x21004b70 and the same remove_timeout callee (FUN_01037f54) as z_add_timeout.

Sets announce_remaining = ticks (0x21004b6c), walks first() of the list at 0x21000750 subtracting dticks, calls t->fn(t) with the lock released, advances curr_tick (0x210044f0), clears announce_remaining, calls sys_clock_set_timeout(next_timeout(), false) and tail-branches to 0x01037438, which stock_call_aliases.ld already binds to z_time_slice - exactly upstream's closing z_time_slice() call.
LOCKED(&timeout_lock) { t = curr_tick + elapsed(); } return t; with the same timeout_lock 0x21004b70, the same curr_tick 0x210044f0 and the same static elapsed() helper (FUN_01037f00).
